text:
Mikhail Sergachev plays 24.6 minutes a night for Utah and has been the defenseman driving the Mammoth's offense: 22 points in 23 games, 13 of them on the power play. Over the last ten his ice time has climbed to 26.2 minutes, a sign of how much the team leans on him through a rough stretch of overtime losses.

Some of the scoring will cool. He has six goals on 3.5 expected goals (the quality of his chances), shooting 10% against 6% last season. The chances are real; that finishing rate rarely lasts. His on-ice luck is close to neutral, though, so the playmaking looks honest.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking backs that up: 6.5 primary shot assists per 60 last season, 94th percentile among defensemen, and he stops 17% of the entries aimed at his blue line against a typical 11%. Evolving-Hockey was cooler on his overall value, 0.7 wins above replacement.

Off the ice, his name keeps coming up next to his old Tampa Bay teammate Nikita Kucherov, with Bolavip reporting Utah as a suitor "aided by Mikhail Sergachev." Treat that as reporting, not fact.
headline: Sergachev is Utah's engine, with a hot stick
